source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 6 (Water Resources).

sections.heading: 1. Water Resources of India
points: India has ~4% of the world's water resources but ~17% of the population → **water stress**.
Sources: **surface water (rivers, lakes, ponds, tanks)** and **groundwater**.
The largest use of water is for **irrigation (agriculture)**, followed by industry and domestic use.

sections.heading: 2. Water Demand and Utilisation
points: Rising demand from **agriculture, industry, and growing population/urbanisation**.
**Groundwater** is over-exploited (falling water table, especially Punjab, Haryana, western UP, Rajasthan).
Uneven distribution — water-surplus and water-deficit regions.

sections.heading: 3. Water Quality and Pollution
points: **Water pollution** from sewage, industrial effluents, fertilisers/pesticides makes water unsafe.
Rivers like the **Ganga and Yamuna** are heavily polluted → **Namami Gange / river action plans**.
Groundwater contamination (arsenic, fluoride, nitrates) is a health hazard.

sections.heading: 4. Water Conservation and Management
points: **Rainwater harvesting and watershed management** recharge groundwater.
**Water recycling and reuse**, drip/sprinkler irrigation (micro-irrigation) improve efficiency.
Traditional systems (tanks, johads, bawaris) and river interlinking are debated.
The **National Water Policy** stresses sustainable, equitable water use.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India = ~4% of world's water, ~17% of population (water stress).
Largest water use = irrigation (agriculture).
Groundwater over-exploited (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan).
Namami Gange = Ganga cleaning; arsenic/fluoride = groundwater contamination.
Conservation: rainwater harvesting, watershed management, drip irrigation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Irrigation (agriculture) is the largest user of water** in India.
**Groundwater is over-exploited** in Punjab/Haryana/Rajasthan (falling water table).
**Namami Gange** is the programme to clean the **Ganga**.
**Drip and sprinkler (micro-irrigation)** improve water-use efficiency.
